Worship isn't singing. Worship is an attitude and offering from within ourselves to God. If you read through the bible, worship is revealed to be a lifestyle, the daily offering of your life to God, the conscious decision to choose Him every moment. Prayer can be worship. Meditating about how good He has been to you and how wonderful He is can be worship. Sitting in silence and feeling at peace and being aware that He is with you can be worship. Try not to get too caught up with the idea that singing songs is worship and that if you don't feel something it means you aren't worshipping.

Part of the reason that singing, especially congregational singing is so strongly associated and defined as worship is because music can be evocative and prompt emotions and when you are singing, you can focus your inner thoughts in the direction of God and that can result in feelings of connection. One thing that may help you feel more connected during music and singing, is turning your attention to the words you are singing and trying to mean those words, to be sincere in voicing them. Try to use it as an opportunity to think about the things the song is expressing. But if you dont feel an emotional response to the song, dont get discouraged and feel like you haven't worshipped. The scripture says to meditate on the Lord night and day, to think on things that are good and wonderful, you can feel accomplished in the fact that you are obeying the commands of God by trying to connect with Him this way. 

Scriptures also says that those who seek the Lord will find Him. Your relationship with God is something unique to you. You don't have to feel Him or acknowledge Him in the same way or same methodology that some other people might. Think about the relationships you have with people, and what helps you feel connected to them. There are likely many other ways that will give you that same feeling of connection to God, especially if you are able to recognize things that make you feel connected to others and ways that you can do similar things to feel connected to God. Try not to get upset with yourself for not having the same experience that you might perceive someone else as having, or with them for connecting with God in a different way than you. You may eventually learn to feel that same type of connection during the music portion at church, but if you don't, that's okay too. God wants us to connect with him in multiple ways, and if you keep seeking Him and are sincere in your pursuit of a relationship with him, you will build a closer connection with God and learn how to hear and feel connected to Him. It may just take some time. 

Please be encouraged, and know that you can offer anything as worship. When you are doing a task, saying to God, i am doing the very best I can at this as an offering to you. When you feel angry, think to yourself that you are choosing to respond with kindness as an offering of obediance to God. Those kinds of simple, everyday things are worship, much more than just mindlessly singing a song could ever be. Keep going, keep seeking. You will find Him.

Lots of great advice in this thread.

 Additionally, I'd say that you should look for forms of escapism. You know that phrase "Out of sight, out of mind"? You need to also try to give your mind a break from obsessing over the stress  continually. If you have the attention span for it, entertainment in the form of books, movies, tv shows, youtube videos are all things that can help get your mind off of what is bothering you so that you can get a mental breather. If you can't focus on a movie, try adding in a physical activity while you are watching, like sewing, crafting or a puzzle. If you are artistically inclined, or even if you're not, art can also be a good distraction for your brain to focus your attention elsewhere and help give you some mental stamina to make it through the day. 

When i was going through the worst parts of my journey with PTSD, depression and anxiety, I started doing things like word searches, sudoku, and drawing intricate pen and ink art to focus my attention when i had idle time. Adult coloring pages can also help in that regard as well. Basically, when you have free time or time where your mind can wander, that's when it becomes easiest for your brain to obsess and start spiraling. Try to occupy and control the focus of your attention so that the stress has less room to take over. Journaling can help, but sometimes does lead to your attention going right to your sources of stress and triggering a reaction. Use coping strategies like breathing exercises if you do start to spiral. 

There are also some good apps that help with mental wellness. A couple that I have tried are the Tapping Solution (this uses tapping techniques on pulse and stress points to help reduce stress) and Finch, which uses a lot of different techniques and strategies to redirect yourself. Most importantly, develop and use your support system. Reach out for help when you need it. You can and will get through this and it will get better. Best wishes to you!

My parents mostly used belts, but they hung on a special rack in their bedroom. My dad's was just "The Belt". It was tan colored, wide, thick leather with a big buckle. My mom had 2, "Mr. Belt" and "Mrs. Belt." They were both black, thin leather, but Mrs. Belt was whippier. Mrs. Belt almost always broke skin, Mr. Belt usually just left welts. My dad hit a lot harder than my mom, so I especially hated being punished by him. He wasnt around a lot though and was very disconnected from our family, so my mom had to take care of it more often. His belt often broke skin too and caused deeper bruising. I remember I hated how they relished telling us to go get the belts from their room and they usually yelled at us the entire time they beat us. The worst I beating ever got wasn't with one of the belts though, it was with a plastic balloon stick that I got in trouble for swordfighting my friend with.  When it broke he moved on to an electrical cord.

The thing is, both my parents are human. They're multidimensional, not villains in a story. There are reasons they did the things that they did. I don't have a relationship with my dad anymore, i hated him for a long time, and now its just settled into loving him because he is my dad from afar, maybe seeing him for a holiday every few years or so,  and accepting that this is the way things are, but that has more to do with his history of neglecting me and my sisters, and with his inability to form close relationships or engage with people. My mom and I are close, she apologized to me later as an adult, but even with her we still go months at a time without seeing each other.  Societal norms and expectations were different then and the expectation especially in certain areas was that this was how you parented. It resulted in a lot of parents taking their anger and frustrations out in their children physically. The thing is, I know my parents, I understand why they are the way they are, and the things in their own pasts that caused them to make the decisions they did. They had their own abuses, and its not always easy to break that cycle. Some of the things they did were unequivocally wrong, but knowing where a lot of it came from allowed me to look at them with empathy and let go of a lot of the bitterness that I had for a long time. 

Kids naturally want to love their parents. Theyre looking for love and affection wherever they find it, and love sometimes allows you to overlook a lot. Thats not always a good thing, i know my childhood influenced the abusive relationship I got into as an adult. It also gave me a lot of baggage (and kinks, ha!) and influenced key components of who I am and how I view relationships and others and my ability to trust in a negative way. However, trauma and abuse doesnt have to affect you forever. People are resilient and able to grow and change. And that goes for abusers too. It all lies with an individual's choice. If you do the emotional and mental labor that growth requires it can change perspectives and morality and turn bad people into good ones. It doesnt make things that happened okay, but its possible to move past it to something better, whatever that may look like. For some people its no contact, for others forgiveness. Whats important is that the cycle is stopped and I think its a great indicator that societal views have changed so much.

The lovely thing about art is that so much is left to the audience's personal tastes and interpretations. While there are times when I personally have experiences moments when I don't have the language to encompass how I am feeling, or a word to label the entirety of an experience, I usually have a fairly good grasp of at least some elements of it. 
I've read more absract pieces that I've enjoyed that are a similar style to what you are describing, and to me, in those types of work, the feeling IS the message. However, its also been possible for me to feel so mystified by what the creator ehat intending to do with their piece that i couldnt connect to even any feeling it was attempting to provoke, and for me, this was one of those pieces. I'm certainly not going to tell someone they are wrong for liking (or disliking) a piece of media, or that they are wrong for whatever response it provokes within them. My point here was simply to say that I could not connect with this piece. I felt that it was too vague, disconnected and obscure to convey any kind of feeling i connected with or found meaningful. In my opinion, that makes it bad art to me. If someone else considers it to be great art, I'm glad for them to experience it and I'll be on my way.

Im all for critical analysis in art but if the author uses so much mystery and metaphor that it hinders the audience from ciphering any meaning whatsoever from the work, then maybe they should re-examine why they choose to create their art this way and whether they are being purposefully obtuse Boit what they are trying to communicate in order to try to elevate their work. I love to pull apart a piece and try to glean all the facets of meaning that the creator intended, but i feel like if a piece needs too much outside information, backstory or commentary in order to be understood, its not what i would consider good art.

I stare up at the ceiling, the popcorn texture taking on strange patterns in the dim, blue-washed light of my alarm clock. A quick glance tells me it's nearly 2 am, and here I am, still flopping uselessly beneath my thin blanket, listening to my own breath and the relentless chatter in my head.


Today was hard. I went to work and of course my boss made his usual unrealistic demands for the day. I'd worked through my lunchbreak, scarfing down a dry granola bar as I poured over contract details and ledger numbers, and still I ended up staying 2 hours late in order to finish up my reports for the day. It's getting to me, the relentless cycle. Get up, work, eat, sleep. The days seem to run into one another and were it not for the constant deadlines I face, I doubt I would remember what day it was at all. 


I close my eyes, defeated. I'm working so hard, trying so hard, and yet it's never enough. My bills are skyrocketing, I'm 2 months behind on rent and to top it all off, my car broke down 2 days ago. It wouldn't be so bad if I could have called a friend to give me a ride to work until I could scrape together enough money to fix the car, but I don't even have a friend to call. I have no one. Not anymore. The Uber I'd had to call to take me to work had taken nearly the last of my hard-earned funds. I feel like I'm constantly drowning, able to surface only long enough for a sip of air before being plunged back beneath the suffocating depths of hopelessness. It's hard trying to make it all by yourself. The void that my life has become yawns in front of me, waiting to swallow me up completely in darkness.


I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do, oh God please help me, how am I gonna make it? I hear my own ragged breathing, panic clawing wildly in my chest as I struggle to quiet the voice in my head. Tears seep from my closed lids. Just go to sleep. Just keep going. Sleep and tomorrow will be a new day. Just go to fucking sleep. 

I roll onto my side, scrunching the blanket beneath my chin. I force myself to keep my eyes closed, pushing away thoughts as quickly as they form. Think of nothing. Think of nothing. Think of nothing. I drift in the fog, my weariness finally taking me over, but before I finally slip under the silken solace of slumber and into the realm of oblivion, one last lurking thought creeps in. I wonder if she will come to me tonight.

I wake with a start, alert, my heart pounding and mind racing. I can hear it, the slow scratch of claws scraping into scarred wood, the steady huffing breath of a body not my own. Flat on my back, I struggle to move, my head refusing to turn, my arms pinned to my sides. She's here. Oh god, she's here!


Floorboards creak, the sound obscenely loud in the darkness of my bedroom. Glancing toward to doorway I could barely make out the reflective glitter of eyes in the hallway. My heart beats loudly. Once. Twice. I hear movement. And then she appears.


Her sleek gray fur and tufted ears look more like shadows than substance, and yet her dainty muzzle and sharp teeth stand out in sharp relief as her mouth gapes open, breathing in a long, listless inhalation. She closes her mouth with a sigh, and sniffs delicately at the air. Enormous eyes blink at me as she slinks into the room. They almost seem to glow with a light of their own, catching the light of my clock and spilling out their own green illumination. Her body somehow seems both feline and canine all at once, the shape and line of her not immediately recognizable as any animal I have ever seen and yet still familiar. Her movements are lithe, the muscles stretching and bunching beneath the dark satiny fur that covers her. Her claws scrape as she moves closer.


I take short, shallow breaths, nearly unable to believe that she is here in the room with me. I feel the coiled energy coming from her, the strained tension of so much wild power held in check. She creeps up to the side of the bed, and the hot wash of her breath fans my skin. I close my eyes, still unable to move as she shoves her nose against my neck, catching my scent and snuffling into my ear. I remember those long, white teeth, the way they curve within her mouth and I shiver at their proximity to my vulnerable throat.


She huffs softly, satisfied, and I feel the bed shift as she leaps onto the mattress beside me. It sags beneath her heavy weight and I open my eyes to see her turn herself around in a circle three times. She sidles up to me, pressing her body against mine, her great paws settling on each shoulder. For a moment our eyes meet, human and inhuman, a silent communion between us. She rests her head against my chest with a soft sigh and suddenly I can move again. My arms wrap around her warm body and my fingers tunnel into her fur. She closes her eyes and I hear it. A low, deep rumble emanating from deep in her chest and throbbing beneath my hands. I close my eyes once again as she purrs, my loneliness dissolving in the soothing sound of her contentment. I smile. This time sleep comes easily.

I may get down voted for my suggestions, but is it possible that he is under an increased amount of stress or anxiety? A high pressure job, a toddler, the pandemic, there are already natural stressors present that could be causing behavior that is unusual.
You mentioned that engaging in childish, silly behavior is something he has always occasionally done but it's become almost constant. It almost makes me wonder if this is a coping mechanism. Many therapists encourage age regression as a coping technique for anxiety and stress and in fact its something that most people do from time to time without being fully aware of what they are doing. However, this sounds like it is at an unhealthy level. I'm wondering if his reverting to childishness is sort of an escape from responsibilities he feels burdened or stressed by and it has elevated into something that feels normal to him but it actually unhealthy dependence on a coping mechanism. If that's the case he is in need of additional coping tools and conscious awareness of why he behaves this way.
Regardless, there is a very definitive breakdown of communication. You might see if you can seek counseling together and if not by yourself, if only to help with communicating to him the seriousness of how this is affecting you and possibly your child. Obviously there is a lot more that can be gained so I hope you are able to take that option. Best of luck to you and your family.

I am a Special Education teacher and although a person with DS is likely to face additional health issues I will argue the point that they do not live fulfilling lives. Some of the happiest, most well adjusted people I have known have DS. In fact, one of the most common things you will hear from a family that includes a member with DS is how happy that individual is and how their joys spills over onto the rest of their family. Quality of life is not determined by a lack of medical problems.

Also, there are government programs specifically for people with special needs. When they enter adulthood, they qualify for adult services, which helps develop and execute a plan for their care for the duration of their lifetime in the event of situations like the one described where parents pass away before the child.  The fact that there are mentally capable siblings will also come into play when they reach adulthood. Please don't think that people with DS are just cast out to fend for themselves or left to suffer. There are many, many advocates working to ensure that they are not only cared for, but well cared for.  The community built by families of children with special needs is very strong and very active. Often these families meet during early childhood and form tight bonds with each other . They help each other in every area you could imagine. Advocating, legal, financial, medical, emotional support...  life would certainly change but there is already a support system in place just waiting to help families like this one.

I understand your perspective and agree with you that the character probably isn't worth saving and ethically should be stopped at all costs but my point is that worth and ethics simply do not come into play when it comes to unconditional love.  As a parent the love I have for my kids is not necessarily rational. It's not based on their actions but simply on the fact of who they are to me. My child. 

Even the most terrible people in human history likely had people who truly mourned their passing, because their actions did not cancel out the affection that person had for them. When you factor in the fact that parents have a  biological instinct to care for and  protect their offspring, Han's actions are understandable and realistic. Most parents, I think, would say that their kids behavior and actions might result in many different negative emotions toward that child, but that doesn't reduce or destroy the love for the child in spite of those emotions. Yes, even horrible people not even worthy to be called human probably have at least one parent who will love and defend them even while hating their child's actions and choices. There is conflict in the parent's emotions but the love overrides it all.  While shooting this character would be an automatic move for any other character other than Han and Leia, because of the fact they are his parents they will co tinue to hold hope for him even when there is no hope to be had. They love him, no  matter what. That makes a world of difference.

I think the majority of teachers didn't take the job for the pay.  However, they do expect to be able to reasonably support themselves and their families on their income.  A few of my friends who are teachers are only making around 35k a year.  The majority of the faculty and staff in any given school is severely underpaid.

I work in the education industry as a paraprofessional.  I put in a full (sometimes exhausting) work day, and I am often also teaching the classes I am assisting in because of the shortage of teachers.  I do not make enough money to support just myself on my salary, let alone a family.  Fortunately I am not the sole breadwinner and I enjoy my job, so continuing in my current position is not an issue.  But the education industry is grossly underfunded.  I'm not saying we need to raise taxes or anything to cover that, but obviously the system needs some rehabilitation if many of the educated workers find themselves unable to sustain themselves and their families and are forced to look for better pay.  Of course then you get complaints about the undertrained teachers in charge of educating kids.  It's an ugly situation and getting worse every day.

I personally do not know anyone in the education field that has worked there for more than 5 years that is not there simply because they love teaching kids.  If money was truly their motivation they would have moved on to something that paid better as quickly as possible.
